episode_summary: June 2019 MakerDAO interview (part 2) with Nik Kunkel on the engineering behind Maker: the next-generation signed-price oracle system and keepers, formal verification and audits of the multi-collateral DAI contracts, upgrade paths, the proposed DAI savings rate, and the TradeShift invoice tokenization pilot.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker used 15 oracles pushing ETH prices, with the smart contract taking their median.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: So right now we have 15 Oracles that are all kind of pushing prices for Ethereum.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel explained that Maker's next-generation oracles sign messages with an asset pair, price and timestamp rather than posting transactions.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: they sign a message. And this message is it has the asset pair name, it has the price and it has a timestamp.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker's oracle gossip network used Scuttlebot.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: the particular one we use is called Scuttlebot

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said the next-generation oracle design cut Maker's costs by about 98 percent.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: what we've managed to do there is actually reduce our costs um by about 98 percent

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said misbehaving oracles would be given a 30-minute timeout as spam protection.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: it can put it on like a 30 minute timeout, you know, and like, you know, if after 30 minutes it says, hey, I'll be your friend again.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said he wanted to turn the oracle system into a staking model with challenge-response slashing, still in progress.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: I want to kind of make it into a staking model, right, where effectively oracles put up stake

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker's dark oracles were individuals who must stay anonymous, while light oracles were public institutions.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: Dark oracles are individuals and it's imperative that they remain anonymous, right?

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said Compound, 0x and Coinbase could run light oracles because their reputations and legal exposure would deter collusion.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: So, for example, you could have Compound be running an oracle, you could have 0x run an oracle

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker held about 2 percent of the total Ethereum supply, just above 2 million ETH, in its smart contracts.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: We have about 2% of the entire Ethereum supply locked up in our smart contracts right now. It's just above 2 million Ether

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker worked closely with Trail of Bits and had about five or six audits in total.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: So Trail of Bits is someone that we work extremely closely with.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said every multi-collateral DAI contract had been formally verified.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: we've actually formally verified all of the multi collateral die contracts, every single piece

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel gave as a formally verified property that DAI could only be withdrawn through the loan repayment function.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: No one should ever be able to withdraw DAI except out of this one function where when you're paying back your loan

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker wrote its formal proofs in the K framework, using KEVM and Manticore.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: basically we used the K framework to kind of write our proofs

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said Trail of Bits' latest audit report came back at about three pages, far shorter than the usual twenty.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: the report was like three pages long that's that's it

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said MKR governance could vote to redeploy the system and hand ownership of DAI and MKR to the new deployment.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: So the MKR governance has the ability to basically redeploy the system, right?

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said single-collateral DAI would run in parallel with multi-collateral DAI for about four to six months.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: that system will run in parallel for about four to six months, those two.

cards.claim: In June 2019 the speakers named Instadap and StableWire among alternative front ends built on Maker's DAI.js.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: So there's Instadap, there's SendWire, or not SendWire.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel predicted regulators would come to love Maker once they saw how transparent it was compared with traditional banking.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: But once they realize how much more transparent this type of system is than the traditional banking sector, I think they're going to fall in love with it.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said rebuilding the financial system on top of decentralized base layers was definitely doable and inevitable.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: rebuilding the financial world on top of this is definitely doable in my opinion like inevitable

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said secondary lending protocols such as Dharma helped stabilize DAI by mirroring Maker's rates.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: All of these secondary lending protocols actually help us stabilize DAI.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel proposed a DAI savings rate paying holders about 6 percent annually, funded by borrower fees.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: why don't we like give people 6% interest annually just for holding die?

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel predicted that in five years DAI users would not interact with Maker's own front end directly.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: I don't see the end, the DAI user in five years from now really interacting with like, you know, the maker front end or anything like that.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker was running a pilot with TradeShift to tokenize invoices.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: So we're working with a partner called TradeShift, and they're one of the largest trade finance kind of companies in the world.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel described a planned invoice-financing flow in which suppliers would be wired dollars within 24 hours of signing over invoices.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: They just know that when they go to trade shift, if they like sign over their invoice, they get dollars wired to their account within 24 hours.

cards.claim: In June 2019 the host argued that the 2008 crisis came from dressing up bad assets, and that rebuilding finance on crypto could repeat it.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I hate to beat the dead horse, but 2008 was the result of dressing up a bunch of crap

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel argued that Maker's economic model reused old central-bank and hedge-fund ideas put on chain.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: the economic model we have in Maker is not something new. It's actually something very old.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said the MKR token was not very liquid, a risk for its role as an insurance product.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: the MKR token is not super liquid right now

cards.claim: Nik Kunkel said his favorite Maker moment was launching DAI in December 2017.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: My favorite moment was when we launched Dye in December of 2017.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker had never had an underwater loan, including during the crash after DAI launched.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: we have never, ever had an underwater loan.

cards.claim: In June 2019 Nik Kunkel said each Maker oracle pulled from about five exchanges and used a volume weighted average price, so one exchange's flash crash did not affect it.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: each oracle itself right is pulling from say like five exchanges and it takes the the volume weighted average price

cards.claim: In June 2019 Corey Petty argued that adding collateral types makes Maker a multivariate problem with exponentially growing complexity.
cards.speaker: Corey Petty
cards.quote: As with any multivariate problem, you have exponential increase of complexity as you increase the number of variables.

cards.claim: In June 2019 a host said he came into the interview as a pure skeptic and left about 75 percent convinced.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: i came in as a pure skeptic intentionally

title: MakerDAO pt. 2 - Nik Kunkel
